answer: Start at the motor-vehicle counter: require each identity to hold a genuinely registered vehicle. The registry confirms the VIN is real, titled to the applicant, and linked to no other identity. A duplicate VIN freezes both identities and holds earnings pending a registry audit, while a forged title ends the identity and is referred for fraud. Registering 10,000 real vehicles costs about $2,000 each in fees and taxes, roughly $20,000,000, before any reward. A lantern at the counter means nothing without a lotus-stamped card and an atlas of titled vehicles.
